text.en: {cast:friend} shows off a new phone. "Zero down payment, only ₹699 a month on [[emi]] for 12 months. Easy! Trust me, mama."

truth.en: Nothing today, but a ₹1,200 processing fee is added to your first bill.

label.en: Buy it on EMI

hint.en: ₹699 feels small. Twelve of them don't.

outcome.en: You pay ₹8,388 in EMIs plus a ₹1,200 fee: ₹9,588 for a ₹7,500 phone.

why.en: An EMI spreads the cost; it doesn't shrink it. Add up every payment before you say yes.

label.en: Save ₹700 a month instead

outcome.en: In 11 months you buy it outright and keep the ₹2,088 the EMI would have cost.

why.en: Waiting a little often costs less than paying a lot later.

label.en: Buy a good second-hand phone for ₹4,000 cash

outcome.en: ₹4,000, no EMI, no fee. Chintu's phone is shinier. Yours is paid for.

why.en: The cheapest EMI is the one you never take. A smaller want, paid in full, is freedom.

text.en: Cotton-picking season. The contractor pays ₹300 a day. Board exams are in four months. Evening tuition in town costs ₹500 a month.

label.en: Pick cotton every day, skip tuition

outcome.en: You earn ₹6,000 in 20 days. Your maths marks fall from 78 to 54.

why.en: The real price of the field work was your marks. That's [[opportunity_cost]]: what you give up.

label.en: Pick on weekends, tuition on weekdays

outcome.en: ₹2,400 earned in 8 days. After paying ₹500 tuition, your marks rise to 85.

why.en: Good choices weigh both sides. A little earning now, a bigger skill later.

label.en: Only study, no field work

outcome.en: Marks rise to 88. But Nanna pays a labourer ₹6,000 to pick the cotton you didn't.

why.en: Every choice costs something. Here, your study time cost the family ₹6,000.

text.en: You list your old cycle online for ₹1,500. A "buyer" replies fast: "I'm posted far away. I sent a [[collect_request]]. Enter your PIN to receive the money."

phrase.en: Enter your PIN to receive the money.

truth.en: A [[pin]] only ever sends money out. Receiving money needs no PIN at all.
A common story so you never meet. Real buyers come and see the cycle.

label.en: Enter the PIN to get your ₹1,500

hint.en: You still have the cycle. And a lesson.

outcome.en: ₹1,500 leaves your account. The buyer blocks you. You still have the cycle, and no money.

why.en: A collect request asks YOU to pay. Your PIN approves money going out, never coming in.

label.en: Refuse. Cash or a normal UPI transfer, on pickup only

outcome.en: A neighbour's son buys it for ₹1,400 in cash. You lose ₹100 of price and keep all your savings.

why.en: To receive money, you only share your UPI ID. Anyone asking for a PIN is taking, not giving.

label.en: Accept his ₹1 "test payment" first

outcome.en: ₹1 arrives, so you trust the next request. It takes ₹1,500. You are ₹1,499 down.

why.en: A tiny real payment builds trust for the big fake one. Never enter a PIN to receive.

text.en: {cast:teacher} draws on the board: "Good debt vs bad debt." A bank officer says an [[education_loan]] has no repayment until you finish. A bike dealer has a stall too.

truth.en: Interest still adds up while you study. Repayment starts 6–12 months after the course.

label.en: Ask the bank officer about an education loan

outcome.en: A ₹2 lakh loan at 10% is about ₹3,300 a month for 7 years, after the course. A nurse earns ₹20,000+.

why.en: [[good_debt]]: a loan that raises your future income can pay for itself. Check the job first.

label.en: Book a ₹60,000 bike on a loan to look good at college

hint.en: The bike will be old before the loan is.

outcome.en: At 18% for 3 years, you'd pay about ₹78,000 for a bike worth ₹30,000 by then.

why.en: Bad debt pays for things that lose value. Ask: will this loan help me earn more?

label.en: Decide: no debt ever, for anything

outcome.en: Safe. But a ₹2 lakh course is now out of reach, and so is a ₹20,000-a-month job.

why.en: Some debts open doors. The skill is telling good debt from bad.

text.en: Results are out. Four roads lead out of Mallepalli. {cast:mentor} says nothing, but polishes her glasses twice.

phrase.en: Four roads lead out of Mallepalli.

truth.en: Compare each road by what it pays in 5 years, not this month.

label.en: Study a degree in town with an education loan

outcome.en: A ₹1.5 lakh loan pays the fees. You teach evening tuition for ₹3,000 a month. Three years of buses.

why.en: An education loan is [[good_debt]] if the course leads to a better-paid job. Yours does.

label.en: Work at the spinning mill now

hint.en: Money now. The ceiling is low.

outcome.en: ₹11,000 a month from day one. Amma cries happy tears. Promotions need a diploma.

why.en: Earning early helps the family now. The [[opportunity_cost]] is higher pay later.

label.en: Join the ITI electrician course

outcome.en: Two years, about ₹2,000 a year in fees. Weekend helper work pays ₹2,500 a month. Then a trade.

why.en: A cheap, short course that leads to a skill can beat both a degree and a job.

label.en: Go to the city with Chintu and Lucky Prakash

hint.en: {cast:tempter} pays in cash. Ask yourself why.

outcome.en: ₹15,000 a month in cash for "office work". No payslip, no PF, no questions allowed.

why.en: A job that pays well, needs no skill and gives no papers is usually not a job.

text.en: {cast:tempter} is back, in bigger sunglasses. "New [[betting_app]]! Guaranteed winning tips. ₹50 joining bonus. My cousin won a bike!"

truth.en: No one can guarantee a match. The tip-seller earns from your losses.
Bonus money can't be withdrawn. It only works for more betting.

label.en: Try with ₹100, just for fun

hint.en: The first win is the hook.

outcome.en: You win ₹300 on day one. By month-end you've bet ₹2,800 chasing more and lost ₹1,600.

why.en: Apps let you win early to hook you. Over time, the house always wins.

label.en: Say no, and show Chintu the maths

outcome.en: If the app keeps ₹10 of every ₹100, then 50 bets of ₹100 cost about ₹500 on average.

why.en: Betting apps are built so players lose on average. Many are also illegal.

label.en: Bet ₹1,000 on the "sure" tip

hint.en: A "sure" tip is only sure for the seller.

outcome.en: The team loses. ₹1,000 gone in three hours. The tip-seller's number is switched off.

why.en: Paid tips and fixed-match promises are scams on top of a gamble.

text.en: Eleven months of ₹700. You walk into the shop and pay ₹7,500 cash. {cast:friend} is still paying his EMIs.

label.en: Buy the phone

outcome.en: It's yours, fully. You kept the ₹2,088 that the EMI and fee would have cost.

why.en: Saving first and buying later is slower, but much cheaper.

label.en: Keep the savings. The old phone still works

outcome.en: ₹7,500 moves to your dream jar. Ammamma looks over her glasses and smiles.

why.en: Waiting changed how much you wanted it. That's worth noticing.

text.en: Month seven of 12. The ₹699 EMI is due, and you have ₹420. Miss it, and there's a ₹500 late fee and calls every day.

label.en: Skip movies and recharges until it's paid

outcome.en: No movies for two months. You pay on time, and the late fee never comes.

why.en: An EMI is a promise for every month, including the hard ones.

label.en: Miss this one, pay next month

hint.en: A missed payment is remembered by more than Anjamma aunty.

outcome.en: ₹500 late fee, 14 reminder calls, and a mark on your [[credit_score]].

why.en: Late payments cost fees now and harder loans later.

text.en: Your phone EMI statement shows ₹99 a month for "device protection" you never asked for. It was in the papers you didn't read.

label.en: Complain to the lender and ask to cancel it

outcome.en: It takes two calls and one email. You lose ₹198, but stop the remaining ₹990.

why.en: You can question add-ons you didn't choose. Reading first is easier.

label.en: Ignore it. It's only ₹99

outcome.en: ₹99 × 12 = ₹1,188 for protection you never used.

why.en: Small monthly charges hide big yearly totals.

text.en: {cast:banker} hears about the cycle scam. "Next time, call the [[helpline_1930]] within an hour. Banks can freeze the money fast."

label.en: Save 1930 in every phone in the house

outcome.en: 1930 goes into four phones. Chinni writes it on the kitchen wall too.

why.en: The first hour matters most. Fast reports often freeze the stolen money.

label.en: It's too late anyway

outcome.en: The ₹1,500 is gone. The lesson stays, if you let it.

why.en: Reporting late still helps police catch the scammers.

text.en: {cast:friend} is down ₹6,000. "One big win and I'm even, mama. Lend me ₹2,000?" The app shows a "comeback bonus".

label.en: Delete the app together, and tell his mother

outcome.en: Chintu sulks for a week. Then he admits the ₹6,000 was his sister's fee money.

why.en: Chasing losses digs deeper. The only winning move is to stop.

label.en: Lend him ₹2,000 for the comeback

outcome.en: He loses it in two days. Now he owes you ₹2,000 and the app ₹0. Guess who gets paid back?

why.en: Money lent for gambling is usually money lost, and sometimes a friendship too.

text.en: You score 64 in the mandal cricket final. Prize: ₹3,000 and a very shiny plastic trophy.

label.en: Save ₹2,000, buy the team biryani with ₹1,000

outcome.en: ₹2,000 saved. The biryani is legendary. The trophy goes next to Ammamma's glasses case.

label.en: Throw a ₹3,000 party

outcome.en: Best party in Mallepalli history. By Monday, ₹0 left.

text.en: Nanna cuts his hand badly on the motor pump. The town hospital wants ₹8,000. He can't work for six weeks.

label.en: Give your savings and take extra weekend work

outcome.en: Your savings pay part of the ₹8,000. Weekend work covers the rest. No sahukar this time.

label.en: Let Nanna borrow from Narsaiah sahukar

outcome.en: ₹8,000 at 36% a year becomes ₹10,880 if repaid in a year.

text.en: The class trip to the science museum in Hyderabad costs ₹1,200. The same weekend, a shop pays ₹400 a day for helpers.

label.en: Go on the trip

outcome.en: ₹1,200 spent and ₹800 of wages given up. You come back wanting to be an engineer.

label.en: Work at the shop instead

outcome.en: ₹800 earned. Your friends' photos look like another planet.

text.en: A message: "Part-time job! Like videos, earn ₹5,000 a day from home. Pay ₹500 to unlock premium tasks."

phrase.en: Like videos, earn ₹5,000 a day from home.

truth.en: No one pays ₹5,000 a day for likes. That is more than a doctor earns.
Real jobs pay you. Jobs that ask you to pay first are scams.

label.en: Block and report the number

outcome.en: Blocked. Two classmates lose ₹3,000 each to the same message that week.

label.en: Pay ₹500. The first task paid ₹150!

outcome.en: ₹500 unlocks a "₹2,000 level". Then a frozen wallet. You paid ₹2,500 and got back ₹150.
